title: Cloud services knowledge base schema
description: Contract for the three data files. The stable layer (types, units) answers what each service is and what it is measured in; the volatile layer (offers) answers who provides it, how much of it, and at what price. All prose in data/ is the canonical English text; Spanish translations live in locales/es/, keyed by the same ids.

dimension.description: Id of the physical or commercial dimension being measured. Its display name lives in locales/<lang>/ui.json under dimensions.

plain_words.description: The same idea without jargon. Required: it is what makes the guide readable by anyone.

handy_equivalent.description: A concrete reference that gives the quantity a sense of scale.

aliases.description: What the industry calls it, so it can be found by searching.

units.description: Units in which this type is measured and billed.

provider_examples.description: Product names; not translated. If an entry is a phrase rather than a name, locales/<lang>/types.json may override the whole array.

limit_type.description: THE KEY DISTINCTION. A monthly pool and a per-request cap are not comparable: the latter makes expensive operations fail even when quota is left over.

plan.description: A concrete tier within a product line (for example a virtual machine size). Lets the whole price table live inside the offer.
Commercial name. null if the provider does not publish one and the plan is identified by its resources alone.

ram_gb.description: If the offer has binary_units, this figure is expressed in GiB.

storage_gb.description: Included disk. null when the provider includes none and charges for it separately, as Fly.io does with its volumes.

transfer_tb.description: null if the provider's table does not publish included transfer. If the provider advertises it as unlimited, use transfer_unlimited: 'not published' and 'no limit' are different things.

transfer_unlimited.description: true when the provider advertises unlimited traffic. It is usually bounded by the link bandwidth, which is the real limit.

network_gbps.description: Link bandwidth. Some providers publish a single figure and others split inbound and outbound as inbound/outbound.

per_second_price_usd.description: Only for providers that bill per second. Its presence means the monthly price is an equivalence, not a ceiling.

type.description: Reference to types.json: it provides the what-it-is and what-it-is-for.

pricing_model.description: Answers 'how long does it last?': by time or by consumption quota.

expires.description: Expiry date or a description of it. null = does not expire.

includes.description: Answers 'what does it offer?', in the units of the type.

plans.description: Tier table of the line, when the provider publishes several sizes.

binary_units.description: true if the provider expresses memory and disk in MiB/GiB instead of MB/GB. A GiB is 7.4 % larger: without this flag, comparisons across providers drift.

pricing_region.description: Region the recorded prices belong to, for providers whose price table varies by region.

confidence.description: 'official' = verified in the provider's own documentation. 'secondary' = another source; treat with caution.

sources.description: Required. A row without a source does not go in.

screenshot.description: Path under sources/ to a capture of the official price table.

integrity_rules: Every type.family must exist in types.json/families
Every unit cited in type.units must exist in units.json
Every offer.type must exist in types.json
Every offer.includes[].unit must exist in units.json
Every offer.pricing_model must exist in offers.json/pricing_models
Every limit_type must exist in units.json/limit_types
Every unit.dimension must exist in locales/<lang>/ui.json/dimensions
Identifiers are unique within their file
Every offer has a verification date and at least one source
i18n: every id in data/ has an entry in locales/es/ and vice versa; lists (aliases, pitfalls, include_notes) have the same length in both languages
